requirement_text.REQ-051: Port src/engine/transition.zig's PARALLEL_GATEWAY branches (EE-06 split / EE-07 join) into REQ-044's transition dispatch. See lib/letflow/design/req051-parallel-gateway-split-join.md for the full design and lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex for the implementation.

task.description: Write tests for REQ-051's 6 acceptance criteria (see acceptance_criteria below, copied verbatim from docs/requirements.yaml) against the implementation in lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex, join_counter.ex, instance_state.ex. Also retire/rewrite the one obsolete test at test/letflow/engine/transition_test.exs:348, which asserted REQ-044's now-retired PARALLEL_GATEWAY stub error -- REVIEWER confirmed (step-02d handoff) this is a genuinely anticipated design consequence, not a regression: a zero-edge PARALLEL_GATEWAY is now correctly classified :pass_through and returns {:error, {:unknown_node_id, node_id}} instead of the old stub error. Either retarget that specific test case to assert the new correct behavior, or split it (a real :pass_through-with-no-edge case plus, if REQ-044-era 'not yet implemented' coverage is still wanted for some other still-stubbed node type, move it there) -- your judgment on the cleanest shape, per REVIEWER's suggestion.
acceptance_criteria: a PARALLEL_GATEWAY with 3 outgoing edges produces exactly 3 tokens with 3 distinct branch_ids in one transition call
a join with 3 expected branches does not fire when 2 tokens have arrived and does fire when the 3rd arrives, asserted at both points

a join whose branch count is 3 but where 1 branch was cancelled via the EE-08 path fires when the remaining 2 active tokens arrive -- it does not wait for the cancelled branch, demonstrated by an explicit test
when every branch of a split is cancelled before any reaches the join, the join node is cancelled and the instance status becomes CANCELLED
tokens arriving at a join in two different orders produce the identical post-join state, and the join fires exactly once in both orderings

a variable key produced with different values on two parallel branches resolves through REQ-049's merge policy with a VARIABLE_OVERWRITTEN event, not through a second collision rule defined in this module
test/letflow/engine/transition_test.exs:348's obsolete REQ-044-stub assertion is retired/rewritten to match the new, correct :pass_through behavior for a zero-edge PARALLEL_GATEWAY node.
